full_judgment:
2. The petitioner is a resident of village Ghashitala, No. 9 Mollargaon Union Parishad, P.S. Kotwali, district Sylhet. He has stated that 6 Union Parishads namely, Khadimpara, Toker Bazar, Mollargaon, Tultiker, Kuchai and Baraikhandi are adjacent to Sylhet Pourashava. The inhabitants of the aforesaid 6 Union Parishads made representations to the relevant authorities on several occasions for declaring the areas covered by those Union Parishads to be Urban area and also for inclusion of the same within Sylhet Paurashava. In response to the aforesaid demand of the said people the respondent No. I issued Notification No. S.R.O. 100-L/86/S- VI/N-11/ 180/142 dated 2.4.86 declaring certain areas adjacent to Sylhet Pourashava as urban area. Thereafter, for the purpose of inclusion of the aforesaid declared urban areas with Sylhet Pourashava objections were invited and after considering the objections and counter-objections of the mhabitants of those areas the respondent No. 1 issued another Notification No. S.R.O.188/Law/87/S.H.A.16/A-11/80-1987dated 8.9.87, cancelling the earlier Notification dated 2.4.86 and making certain modifications as regards the urban areas. According to the subsequent Notification dated 8.9.87 published under section 3(1) of the Pourashava Ordinance, 1977 (hereinafter referred to as Pourashava Ordinance) the area of entire Tultiker Union Parishad and major portions of the above- named five Union Parishads were declared as urban area. 

 3. On 24.10.88 a Gazette Notification No. SHA-II/20-5/88/234 (Annexure E) was published purportedly under sections 19 and 24 of Pourashava Ordinance, by which the respondent No. 1 declared the number of wards, demarcation of wards and number of Commissioners to be elected from each ward of Sylhet Pourashava, excluding the areas which were declared as urban areas by Gazette Notification dated 8.9.87. Thereafter, the Election Commission issued another Notification on 12.12.88 (Annexure H) fixing the election schedule of all Pourashavas of the country including Sylhet Pourashava from 3.1.89 to 28.1.89. It is also stated that the areas which were declared by the notification dated 8.9.87 as urban areas were kept in the previous Union Parishads and elections of those Union Parishads were held on 10.2.88. Challenging the holding of election in the aforesaid urban areas of 6 Union Parishads under Local Government (Union Parishads) Ordinance, 1983 (hereinafter referred to as Union Parishad Ordinance) a writ petition has been filed in this Court which is pending for hearing. Challenging the above notifications dated 24.10.88 and 12.12.88, vide Annexures E and H respectively, the petitioner moved this writ application before this Court and obtained the present Rule. 

 10. In such a situation the proviso to section 3(1) is the appropriate provision to be followed for those 6 Union Parishads whose certain areas have been just declared as urban areas, but not yet included within the Sylhet Pourashava under section 4. If we read carefully section 3, it becomes quite clear that as soon as a rural area is declared as urban area, it will not be a part of the Pourashava ipso facto. It requires further legal steps and ultimate Notification as contemplated under section 4 read with the Rules made thereunder for making it a part of Pourashava. a Unless and until such a Notification is finally published as required under section 4, the areas of the old union parishads, though declared as urban area, will continue and remain under the Union Parishad and for the purpose of election, in our opinion, those Union Parish ads will be guided by the Union Parishads Ordinance, 1983. In view of the above we find little substance in the first contention of Mr. Hannan. 

 12. Mr. Hannan lastly submits that the inhabitants of those areas which have been declared as urban areas are in a precarious position. They arc not getting any advantage or privilege or benefit of the Pourashava. They are living neither as residents of Pourashava nor as residents of Union Parishad. So, considering the conditions of the people of those are as and the precariousness of their political position, they should be allowed to take part in the Pourashava election. Such a contention is absolutely unacceptable, because relevant laws have not made any provision to include those areas even provisionally within the Pourashava till those areas are finally included into Pourashava under section 4. The alleged existing precarious conditions of the people of the area are not to be considered in this forum. It is absolutely within the demain of the concerned authorities of the Government as to how to redress the above grievances of the people.
